qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High-voltage subsea cables enjoy qualification barriers and oligopoly supply dynamics, but standard building wire and distribution cables face commodity competition. Subsea cable installation requires heavy capital expenditure, keeping multi-year GAAP ROIC below the 12% hurdle (~8.6-10.2%) with operating margins around 5-6%.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). French cable manufacturer pivoting to pure-play electrification. Despite high-voltage grid interconnector tailwinds, commoditized low-voltage cables and high capex on subsea installation vessels hold multi-year GAAP ROIC to ~8.6-10.2% (below the 12% threshold) with low operating margins (~5-6%).
qualitative.evidence: Multi-year GAAP ROIC has tracked ~8.6% to 10.2% across 2022-2025, falling short of the 12% hurdle. Operating margin (EBIT / sales) hovers at 5-6%. Heavy capital intensity from specialized cable-laying vessels (e.g. Nexans Aurora, Electra) and large turnkey contract execution risks dilute economic returns.
